question: What is the primary goal of occupational health hazard control measures?

options.B: Punishing workers who ignore safety protocols
options.C: Increasing daily factory and hospital output
options.D: Reducing compensation payout costs for employers

explanation: The main objective of any control measure is stopping harm before it happens to workers. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why are Nigerian healthcare workers considered at risk for biological hazards?

options.A: Inhaling toxic fumes from chemical plants
options.B: Working long shifts without adequate lighting
options.D: Exposure to infectious agents like Lassa virus

explanation: Biological hazards specifically refer to living organisms and pathogens that cause disease in healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which level is considered the most effective in the hierarchy of hazard controls?
explanation: Getting rid of the hazard completely removes the risk of exposure at the source. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: Why is personal protective equipment placed at the bottom of the control hierarchy?

options.A: It relies on human behavior and fails if damaged
options.B: It is the most expensive option for employers
options.C: It eliminates the hazard completely from the site
options.D: It requires government approval before purchase

explanation: PPE does not remove the hazard and leaves room for user error or equipment failure. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: What is the key difference between elimination and substitution?

options.A: Elimination removes the hazard, while substitution replaces it
options.B: Elimination uses PPE, while substitution uses engineering
options.C: Elimination applies only to biological hazards
options.D: Substitution is more expensive than elimination

explanation: Elimination gets rid of the danger entirely, whereas substitution swaps a bad substance for a safer one. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: A hospital replaces toxic glutaraldehyde with a safer enzymatic detergent for instrument sterilization. What strategy is this?
explanation: Exchanging a dangerous chemical for a less harmful option describes substitution. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of engineering controls over personal protective equipment?

options.A: They completely eliminate all workplace hazards
options.B: They require no maintenance over their lifetime
options.C: They are always cheaper to install initially
options.D: They do not rely on constant worker compliance

explanation: Engineering controls work automatically without needing the worker to remember to put them on. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: Installing a local exhaust hood over a laboratory workbench to suck away chemical fumes is an example of what?
explanation: Physical equipment changes like ventilation hoods fall under engineering controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an administrative control?

options.A: Issuing thick earmuffs to machine operators
options.B: Replacing a toxic paint with a water-based brand
options.C: Rotating workers to limit exposure time to loud noise
options.D: Installing soundproofing materials around a noisy generator

explanation: Job rotation alters work organization schedules, which is an administrative measure. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: Why are administrative controls considered less reliable than engineering controls?

options.A: They are too expensive for small Nigerian businesses
options.B: They physically remove hazards from the workplace
options.C: They depend on human compliance and consistent enforcement
options.D: They only apply to biological agents in hospitals

explanation: If workers or managers fail to follow the rules, administrative controls break down easily. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: Where does personal protective equipment rank in the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: Equal to engineering and administrative controls
options.C: At the bottom as the last line of defense
options.D: At the top as the most effective strategy

explanation: PPE is used only when other higher-level controls cannot fully eliminate or reduce the hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: A nurse cares for a patient with airborne tuberculosis. What is the most critical aspect of using a respirator in this context?

options.A: Ensuring a proper face seal and correct fitting
options.B: Wearing two masks simultaneously for double safety
options.C: Washing the disposable respirator after every shift
options.D: Selecting a brightly colored mask for easy identification

explanation: A respirator only protects against airborne pathogens if it seals tightly against the face without leaks. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of occupational health surveillance in the workplace?

options.A: Firing workers who fail their annual fitness tests
options.B: Detecting early signs of disease and checking control effectiveness
options.C: Calculating the daily profit margins of the company
options.D: Complying with insurance claims for workplace injuries

explanation: Surveillance tracks worker health trends to catch occupational illnesses early and evaluate safety measures. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why is baseline medical screening performed before a worker starts a hazardous job?

options.A: To test the worker's academic qualifications for the role
options.B: To determine the appropriate salary scale for the employee
options.C: To prove the employer is not responsible for future illnesses
options.D: To establish the worker's health status prior to potential exposure

explanation: Baseline checks give a reference point to compare against during later periodic health screenings. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: What is an occupational health nurse doing when performing a walkthrough survey?

options.A: Distributing salary wages to factory workers on payday
options.B: Checking employee attendance registers for absenteeism
options.C: Systematically inspecting the workplace to identify potential health hazards
options.D: Cleaning up hazardous chemical spills on the factory floor

explanation: A walkthrough survey is a visual inspection used by nurses to spot safety risks in a work environment. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)

question: An occupational health nurse notices market traders lifting heavy loads with poor spinal posture. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Reporting the market association to the police for criminal negligence
options.B: Demanding that all traders close their shops until machinery is bought
options.C: Conducting health education on safe lifting and ergonomic body mechanics
options.D: Issuing heavy industrial back braces to every single trader

explanation: Education and training are practical first steps nurses take to address ergonomic risks in informal settings. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)
